title: Exploring Our Town and Buildings
summary: Practise words for town buildings and describe them in English.
keyIdeas: Use 'there is' for one place and 'there are' for several places.
Buildings have different uses: read books in a library and buy bread in a bakery.
Use 'next to', 'opposite' and 'between' to describe where buildings are.

activities.prompt: Match each building with what you can do there.
activities.explanation: You can read and borrow books at a library, watch films at a cinema, see a doctor at a hospital and buy bread at a bakery.

activities.prompt: Aisha needs to buy apples, milk and rice for dinner. Where does she go? 🍎
activities.explanation: A supermarket sells food and things for the home.
activities.hint: Think of a large shop that sells food.

activities.prompt: You can borrow storybooks and study quietly at the fire station.
activities.explanation: False. A library is the place to borrow books and study quietly. A fire station is where firefighters work.

activities.prompt: Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
activities.explanation: Use 'There is' with one thing: 'a big park'. For several parks, use 'There are'.
activities.sentence: There ___ a big park with swings near my school.

activities.prompt: Sort these places by their main use in this activity.
activities.explanation: A cinema, park and museum are places to enjoy activities. A supermarket, bakery and bookshop are shops where you buy things.

activities.prompt: Omar sees smoke coming from a window. He tells an adult. Which emergency workers put out fires? 🚒
activities.explanation: Firefighters put out fires. In an emergency in Spain, call 112 and follow an adult's help.

activities.prompt: Complete the sentence with the preposition meaning 'in the middle of two places'.
activities.explanation: Use 'between' for something in the middle of two places, such as the school and the library.
activities.hint: There is a building on each side of the bakery.
activities.sentence: The bakery is ___ the school and the library.

activities.prompt: Put the words in order to make a correct sentence.
activities.explanation: For the plural, start with 'There are', followed by the number, adjective, building and place: 'There are two modern museums here.'

activities.prompt: Read the text about Lucía's town and answer the questions.
activities.explanation: Find the buildings and the activities Lucía describes in her town.
activities.title: My Town: Greenhill
activities.text: Hello! My name is Lucía and I live in Greenhill. Greenhill is a small and quiet town. In my town, there is a big school with a colourful playground. Next to the school, there is a bakery. The baker makes delicious cakes and warm bread every morning. Opposite the bakery, you can find a quiet library. I often go there on Fridays to read adventure books. We also have a lovely park with green trees and flowers. In the centre, there is a hospital and a police station. I love my town because everything is close and people are friendly.

questions.prompt: What building is directly opposite the bakery?
questions.explanation: The text places the quiet library opposite the bakery.

questions.prompt: Why does Lucía visit the library on Fridays?
questions.explanation: Lucía goes there on Fridays to read adventure books.

activities.prompt: Hugo leaves the cinema. He walks past the park and stops to take a train to visit his cousins. Where is he? 🚆
activities.explanation: To take a train, go to the train station.
activities.hint: This is the place where trains leave from.
